text: The Anti-Breakthrough (Micro-Dosing): If long therapy sessions leave you more overwhelmed than helped, that's actually normal. Dr. Perry explains that a dysregulated brain's "therapeutic window" is often only seconds long, so a sensitized, armored nervous system just can't take in sixty minutes of trauma processing. So for now we need to give up the therapy ideal of the "hour-long breakthrough."
section: Psychology is the Software; Biology is the Hardware.
reader: someone with trauma, often with addiction, who has done therapy and still reacts the same way, reading to learn why and whether this protocol is for them
